$comment: The single source of truth for containerising the Stoatworks web fleet.
scripts/gen-docker.mjs reads this and writes Dockerfile, .dockerignore,
docker-compose.yml, docker/nginx.conf and .github/workflows/docker.yml into
each repo. scripts/gen-templates.mjs reads it and writes templates/*.xml for
Unraid Community Applications. Nothing here is inferred at generation time —
if a build command or output directory is wrong it is wrong *here*.
kind:
static-prebuilt  the served directory is committed; no build stage at all.
static-build     a Node build stage produces the served directory.
node-service     a long-running Node server.
rust-service     a long-running Rust binary.
python-service   a long-running Python server. Only ever paired with
hasOwnDocker: no Python Dockerfile is generated, and the
kind exists so the template reads the app's real port.
cpp-service      a long-running C++ binary. Same deal as python-service:
only ever paired with hasOwnDocker, and exists so the
template reads the app's real port rather than 80.
notFound:
spa       try_files ... /index.html   (mirrors not_found_handling = 'single-page-application')
404page   error_page 404 /404.html    (mirrors not_found_handling = '404-page')
none      plain 404
hostNetwork: true means the app discovers devices with mDNS/broadcast, which
Docker's bridge network does not reliably forward. Bridge mode does not error,
it just finds nothing — so this is not a preference, it is a correctness flag.

apps.title: PMSE to WWB
apps.desc: Turns an Ofcom PMSE licence schedule PDF into Shure Wireless Workbench import files. The PDF is parsed on the server and is not stored.
apps.note: This was a static-prebuilt image serving site/ until 2026-08-05, and that was wrong: site/ is a four-file LANDING page pointing at RFutils, not the app. The app is backend/ (FastAPI, uvicorn on 8000) plus frontend/, and the repo's own Dockerfile has always built it. Generating over that replaced a working converter with a signpost. hasOwnDocker now leaves the Dockerfile and compose alone, and the kind exists only so the template reads port 8000 rather than the 80 a static kind forces — nothing generates a Python image, and nothing needs to.

apps.title: Aspect Calc
apps.desc: Aspect ratio, pixel pitch and screen geometry calculator. Runs entirely in the browser.

apps.title: Blend Calc
apps.desc: Projector edge-blend calculator with Resolume export. Runs entirely in the browser.

apps.title: Test Card
apps.desc: Generates test-pattern PNGs from an output map. Runs entirely in the browser.

apps.title: Otter EDID Editor
apps.desc: Builds and edits EDIDs, and checks them against event video processors. Runs entirely in the browser.

apps.title: Thumbnail Generator
apps.desc: Builds labelled source thumbnail cards for a multiviewer, downloaded as a ZIP. Runs entirely in the browser.

apps.title: ArrayCAD
apps.desc: Converts CAD drawings to d&b ArrayCalc and Soundvision venue data. Runs entirely in the browser.

apps.title: Stagewash
apps.desc: Stage lighting coverage calculator. Project data never leaves the browser.

apps.title: simpleRTA
apps.desc: Real-time analyser, spectrograph and meter. Audio is captured and analysed in the page and never leaves the browser.
apps.note: The CSP in public/_headers allows microphone capture from 'self' only. Serving this over plain HTTP from a non-localhost address will make the browser refuse microphone access regardless of the CSP — getUserMedia requires a secure context. Put it behind your reverse proxy's TLS if you want it on the LAN.

apps.title: Pixel Peeker
apps.desc: LED wall designer and capacity calculator. Runs entirely in the browser.

variants.title: Pixel Peeker Lite
variants.desc: Pixel Peeker without the NovaStar export path. Runs entirely in the browser.

apps.title: ATEM Scopes
apps.desc: Waveform, vectorscope and histogram for a captured video source. Analysis happens in the page and video never leaves the browser.
apps.note: buildCmd is `static:build`, NOT `build`. In this repo `npm run build` is `electron-vite build` and produces the desktop app, not the static site — it would populate out/ and leave dist/ stale or absent, and the image would either fail to copy or silently serve an old build.

apps.title: ATEM Overseer
apps.desc: Fleet dashboard for Blackmagic ATEM switchers — status, health and restreaming across every switcher on the network.
apps.note: packages/server/src/discovery.ts uses multicast-dns. Bridge networking silently discovers nothing, so the template ships host networking. Devices can still be added by IP in bridge mode if you prefer isolation.

apps.title: RFutils
apps.desc: RF coordination toolkit — scanning, frequency planning and wireless monitoring in one server.
apps.note: Discovers receivers over the LAN, so the template ships host networking. Port is read from RFUTILS_SERVER_PORT (falling back to PORT, then 8420).

apps.title: caspar-AV
apps.desc: CasparCG show control server — cue lists, AMCP bridging and OSC control.
apps.note: Two things a Rust-only Dockerfile gets wrong here. `web/` is NOT tracked in git — console/vite.config.ts builds into ../web with emptyOutDir — so the image needs a Node stage before the Rust one or it ships a server whose ServeDir points at nothing and 404s every page. And `--web` defaults to the relative path `web`, which resolves against the working directory, so the runtime stage passes an absolute /app/web rather than relying on WORKDIR.

apps.title: SRT Router
apps.desc: Crosspoint router for SRT video streams, with a web control UI.
apps.note: Built with default features. NDI is included but loads its runtime with dlopen at run time, so the image links no NDI SDK and ships no NDI runtime — the NDI transport is simply unavailable inside the container unless you mount a runtime yourself. The `omt` feature is left off deliberately: omt-io still links its SDK at build time, and that SDK is not redistributable.

apps.title: flock
apps.desc: Discovers and controls networked AV devices from one dashboard.
apps.note: This repo already had a hand-written Dockerfile and docker-compose.yml before this fleet sweep, and they are better informed than anything generated — in particular the note about Debian's ffmpeg possibly lacking SRT input support. The generator does NOT overwrite them. Only the CA template and the GHCR workflow are added here.

apps.title: unfuckarr
apps.desc: Scans a Sonarr/Radarr library, checks every video file is intact and will direct play in Emby, and fixes what is not — transcoding, remuxing, or deleting and re-searching. Deletes go to a recycle bin first.
apps.note: All three hasOwn* flags are set and each is load-bearing. hasOwnDocker: the image is a Python service with ffmpeg and a PUID/PGID entrypoint, which no generated kind produces. hasOwnWorkflow: the repo's CI runs a 78-test suite, builds multi-arch on tags, boots the image and asserts /health, and cuts the GitHub release — a generated docker.yml alongside it would race it to the same tags. hasOwnTemplate: the template needs fifteen Config blocks (media and downloads paths, PUID/PGID/UMASK/TZ, six env seeds, a /dev/dri device) that this generator cannot express; re-expressing them here would split the descriptions from the app they describe.

apps.title: WebLinked
apps.desc: Renders a web page offscreen at a broadcast raster and exact frame rate and sends it out as NDI — a dashboard, scoreboard or clock becomes a source a vision mixer can take.
apps.note: Packaging only — this repo holds no source. Its Dockerfile clones stoatworks-labs/weblinked at build time. All three hasOwn* flags are load-bearing. hasOwnDocker: a multi-stage build that fetches a pinned 315 MB CEF distribution and compiles C++, which no generated kind produces. hasOwnWorkflow: the build takes ~20 minutes and is amd64-only on purpose (arm64 would be QEMU-emulated for a full Chromium-wrapper compile), and its smoke test boots the image and asserts the headless render path is alive — a generated docker.yml would race it to the same tags. hasOwnTemplate: eleven Config blocks, and the NDI runtime mount needs an explanation the generator cannot carry. NOTE the libndi rule: it is dlopen'd and its licence forbids the modification and reverse engineering MIT cannot forbid, so it is NEVER baked into the image — the template mounts it at /opt/ndi/lib from a directory the user supplies.
